description.en: Read the fund part of a FundsXML document: control data, the fund with its identifiers, static data like costs, the net asset value, and the share classes with their prices and amounts in several currencies. Check an ISIN with FreeXmlToolkit.

say.en: In this video you read the fund data of a FundsXML document: the fund, its net asset value and its share classes. It takes about four minutes.

Every delivery starts with ControlData. The ContentDate is the date the data refers to. The DataSupplier names who sends it, here an asset manager from Austria. And DataOperation INITIAL means: this is a first delivery, not a correction.
Below Funds comes the fund itself. It is identified by its LEI, the global Legal Entity Identifier. It has an official name and a fund currency, here euro.

The SingleFundFlag decides the structure. True means a single fund, whose share classes follow directly. False means an umbrella fund, which contains subfunds, and each subfund has its own share classes.
FundStaticData holds what rarely changes: the inception date, and the ongoing costs of one point eight percent, with their publication date.

FundDynamicData holds what changes with every valuation. The total net asset value on the first of October is one hundred twelve point five million. Every amount in FundsXML carries its currency in the attribute ccy.

Further down are the share classes. The first one has its own ISIN, and its currency is the US dollar. Its price is the net asset value per share, one hundred forty-two dollars and eighty-seven cents, with six hundred thousand shares outstanding.
Its net asset value is given twice: in the fund currency, euro, and in the share class currency, dollar. FundsXML allows an amount in several currencies, so nobody has to convert it again.

Is the ISIN of this share class correct? Open the FundsXML panel, and type it into the identifier checker. The checker knows the structure and the check digit of ISINs and LEIs. This one is valid. The letters A T in front stand for Austria.
Change a single digit, and the check digit no longer fits. Typing errors like this are caught before the data goes anywhere.
Thanks for watching. In the next video, you look at the portfolio and the asset master data. The links are on the screen and in the description below.
